svg.text: BEST FOR: TOOL DEFINITIONS AGENTS USE WELL
FORMAT LINEAGE: Anthropic (Writing effective tools) • Brij Kishore Pandey (5-Layer Claude Code ADK & SKILL.md)
Tool Spec Clinic: The Same Tool, Written So an Agent Fails With It — and Written So It Succeeds
Anthropic's tool-writing guide + Brij Kishore Pandey's 5-Layer Claude Code ADK & SKILL.md standard: descriptions and response shapes matter as much as the API.
BEFORE — what most teams ship (the agent guesses)
// UUIDs instead of names, no paging,
'search' collides with three other tools — the agent picks the wrong one a third
No guidance on when (not) to use it, no example, no defaults.
40 KB responses flood the context window; UUIDs force extra lookups.
'Error 500' gives the agent nothing to act on, so it retries blindly.
AFTER — written for the agent that will read it
"description": "Find open or merged PRs in ONE repo by
text, label, or author. Use for 'which PRs touch X'.
Do NOT use for issues (github.search_issues) or
// response: title, number, author NAME, url, 1-line summary;
// error: "repo not found: did you mean acme/auth-service?"
Namespaced name + 'use for / do not use for' + an example — the model routes
Enums and defaults remove invalid calls; required fields are explicit.
Concise mode + pagination keep each result under ~1K tokens; names instead of
Errors tell the agent what to do next — the difference between a fix and a retry
Build for the workflow the agent needs,
Prefix by service and resource so
Names over UUIDs, summaries over dumps;
next_page_token; make errors say what to
do instead of a status code.
onboarding; test on real tasks; let the
Anthropic let Claude rewrite its own tool descriptions from failed transcripts — and accuracy went up. Pair with SKILL.md progressive disclosure.
